title: General Ordinances for B.Tech & B.Tech (Honors)
text:
O.1 Each academic session is divided into two regular semesters (Odd: mid July-Nov, Even: Jan-mid May) and two vacation semesters (winter ~4 weeks, summer ~8 weeks), following a Senate approved schedule.
O.2 Admission to B.Tech. Degree program is made from qualified candidates of JEE (Mains) through CSAB and JoSAA.
O.3 Admission to a particular branch of study is decided by JoSAA.
O.4 Duration of B.Tech / B.Tech (Honors) is minimum 8 semesters (4 years) and maximum 12 semesters (6 years / max period 7 years under Reg 2.3).
O.5 Students can opt for B.Tech. (Honors) at the end of the 4th semester subject to Senate conditions.
O.6 Award of B.Tech / B.Tech (Honors) degree shall be in accordance with Senate approved regulations.

title: Eligibility for Admission & Duration of Program
text:
1.1 Admission is as per MHRD/MoE guidelines with reservations for SC, ST, OBC, PwD, EWS.
1.2 Admissions made in odd semester at 1st year level based on JEE (Mains) rank via JoSAA.
1.3 If misinformation or unfulfilled requirements are found at any time, admission can be cancelled by Senate.
1.4 Institute reserves right to cancel admission on grounds of indiscipline or misconduct. Medical fitness is required.
2.1 Duration: 4 academic years (8 regular semesters of ~20 weeks each: Odd Sem mid-July to Nov, Even Sem Jan to mid-May, winter break ~4 weeks, summer break ~8 weeks).
2.3 Maximum period for completion of B.Tech. program is seven (7) years.

title: Fee Structure & Programs of Study
text:
3.1 Fee structure is decided by competent authority.
3.2 Fee Payment Window:
- Odd Semester: 1 - 30 June (Deadline: 30 June).
- Even Semester: 1 - 31 December (Deadline: 31 December).
All students, including those availing bank loans, must pay fees by the deadline.
4. B.Tech degree programs are offered in specializations specified by engineering schools as per UG curriculum.

title: Structure of Program & Credit Distribution
text:
5.1 Credit Distribution for regular B.Tech (Total: 160 Credits):
1. Major (Core): 75 credits
2. Minor (Stream): 18 credits
3. Multi-disciplinary: 19 credits
4. Ability Enhancement: 9 credits
5. Skill Enhancement: 16 credits
6. Value Added Courses: 8 credits
7. Project: 15 credits (Semesters VI, VII, VIII)
8. Internship: 10 credits (VIII semester in lieu of project requirements for eligible students)
Total for Regular B.Tech = 160 Credits.
Honours/Online Optional Courses: 12 credits.
Total for B.Tech with Honors = 172 Credits.
5.3 Interdisciplinary projects allowed (max 3 students team across departments with HoD permission). Elective withdrawal allowed within 2 weeks from semester start.
Honors Eligibility: GPA >= 8.5 in each of the first four semesters. Must maintain GPA >= 8.5 across all 8 semesters. NPTEL/SWAYAM courses must be passed with Elite or above certificate.

title: Minor Degree Rules & Eligibility
text:
5.4 Minor Degree:
- Ordered sequence of 5 courses (18-20 credits) in a domain outside the major discipline, spread from 4th to 8th semester.
- Credits earned in Minor are in addition to 160 major credits.
5.5 Eligibility for Minor:
- Registration in 4th semester for students with CGPA >= 7.5 up to 3rd semester, with all courses passed in ONE attempt without grace.
- Maximum ONE Minor track allowed.
5.6 Minor Degree Award Rules:
- Must complete all courses in the chosen minor track in ONE attempt.
- If student fails any minor course, minor registration ceases (not eligible for minor degree, but regular degree unaffected; passed credits recorded as Extra Credits on mark sheet).
- Minor degree must be completed simultaneously with major degree (cannot be earned later).
- Separate CGPAs are calculated and mentioned on mark sheet for Major and Minor.

title: Course Plan & Assessments
text:
5.7 Course Plan:
- Details course overview, objectives, outcomes, teaching-learning activities, assessment methods, and compensation policy.
- Number of assessments per course ranges from 4 to 6 (group tasks, quizzes, assignments, open book tests, lab exercises, mini-projects, end-semester exam).
- Students missing an assessment for genuine/emergency reasons may be granted ONE compensation assessment as per absentee schedule.
- Approved by Class Committee (CC) chairperson and HoD.

title: Attendance Policy, Mandatory 75%, Shortage Grades (L & R), Leave Rules & On-Duty
text:
6.1 Mandatory Requirement: 75% attendance is mandatory for all courses (except in cases of medical/sports/institute representing, etc.).
6.2 Consequence of Shortage: Students having less than 75% attendance in any course SHALL NOT BE PERMITTED to appear for the end semester examination in that course.
6.3 Continuous Assessment: Minimum 75% attendance required to be eligible for continuous assessment exams.
6.4 Shortage Attendance Grades:
- 55% to 75% Attendance: Awarded 'L' Grade (Lack of Attendance). The student must complete the attendance criteria by attending required classes before course instructor during semester breaks (if offered) and get an attendance completion certificate to appear in the supplementary exam.
- Less than 55% (<55%) Attendance: Awarded 'R' Grade (Redo). The student MUST re-register for the course in the next academic year and repeat the entire course.
6.5 Short Duration Absence (up to 9 days):
- For absence of maximum 9 days (inclusive of prefixing and suffixing weekends), submit leave application to concerned HoD with supporting documents.
- HoD shall grant leave. Consolidated attendance is calculated by REMOVING this period of leave (denominator reduced). Admissible ONCE per semester.
6.6 Long Duration Absence (> 9 days):
- Prior application through HoD to Dean-Academic Affairs with supporting documents.
- Granted if aggregate attendance was at least 75% at time of applying.
- If permitted student's attendance still remains below 75%, a 5% relaxation may be granted (lowering requirement to 70%).
6.7 Unnotified Absence > 6 Weeks: If absent for more than 6 weeks without notifying Dean-Academic Affairs, registration for that semester stands CANCELLED.
6.8 On-Duty (OD) Attendance: Representing the Institute in approved extracurriculars (Sports, Games, Cultural meets, Seminars, Workshops, Conferences, CCPD Interviews, NCC/NSS Camps) is considered 'on-duty' with prior HoD permission. Period of absence is COUNTED AS 'PRESENT' for attendance computation.
6.10 Elective Change: Marked absent in newly registered elective for duration of attending classes in previously registered elective.

title: Faculty Mentor, Registration & Class Committee
text:
7. Faculty Mentor (FM): Assigned in 1st year, guides student until graduation, meets 2-3 times/semester, maintains Student Appraisal Records (STAR).
8. Registration & Enrolment: First working day of every semester is registration day. Must clear all dues (Institute, Hostel, Library) to be eligible for enrolment.
9. Class Committee (CC):
- Constitution: Chairperson (faculty not teaching that class), all course teachers, and 4 nominated student members.
- Meets 3 times per semester: 1st meeting within 1 week of semester start; 2nd meeting after 6 weeks; 3rd meeting after 10 weeks to review feedback and assessment progress.

title: Assessment Procedure, Theory & Lab Weightages, Integrated Courses & Projects
text:
10.1 Typical Assessment Weightages:
A. Theory Courses (100%):
- Continuous Assessment (quizzes/tests/assignments, min 2): 20%
- Mid-Term Examination (90 minutes): 30%
- End-Semester Examination (180 minutes): 50%
B. Lab Courses (100%):
- Continuous Assessment (programming/demos/assignments, min 2): 40%
- Lab File / Record: 10%
- End-Semester Exam / Viva (180 minutes): 50%
10.2 Integrated Courses (Theory + Lab):
- Evaluation based on credit ratio (e.g., for 4-credit 3-0-2 course, Lab is 25% and Theory is 75%).
10.4 Project Work Evaluation:
- Evaluated by Project Monitoring Committee (PMC: HoD/nominee, coordinator, guide).
- Continuous supervisor assessment: 20%
- Mid-Semester Review (6-8 weeks from start): 40%
- Final Viva-Voce: 40% (with internal/external examiner from IISc/IITs/NITs/IIITs/Govt labs).

title: Grading System, Relative vs Absolute, Passing 30% End-Sem Rule, Supplementary Exams
text:
11. Absentee Assessment: Genuine reasons get compensation test. End-sem absence results in 'ABS' grade and loss of weightage.
12. Performance Analysis Committee (PAC): Meets within 7 days of last exam to finalize grade ranges and submit to Dean Academic.
13. Grading System:
- Letter Grades & Grade Points: S (10 - Outstanding), A (9 - Excellent), B (8 - Very Good), C (7 - Good), D (6 - Average), E (5 - Marginal), I (0 - Incomplete), L (Lack of Attendance), R (Redo Course), M (Malpractice), ABS (Absent).
- Relative Grading: Followed for classes with >= 30 students. Passing cut-off is X_bar / 2 (half of class mean). Students scoring above cut-off placed in top 6 bands (S to E: 10%, 15%, 25%, 25%, 15%, 10% typically). Below cut-off gets 'I' grade.
- Absolute Grading: Used if class strength < 30 students: S (>=85), A (75-84), B (65-74), C (55-64), D (45-54), E (35-44), I (<=34).
- MANDATORY 30% PASS CRITERIA: A student MUST score at least 30% marks in the End-Semester Examination to be awarded any passing grade. Scoring <30% in end-sem results in an 'I' grade automatically.
- Supplementary Examinations: Conducted 1 week prior to registration of next semester for students with 'I', 'L', 'M', and 'ABS' grades.

title: Transparency, Re-evaluation, Break of Study, SGPA/CGPA & Degree Requirements
text:
14. Transparency in Assessment: Students can review evaluated answer scripts within 2 weeks of reopening. Answer scripts retained for 2 academic years for audit.
15. Temporary Break of Study: Allowed with Dean Academic approval on HoD recommendation. Governed by rules in force upon rejoining.
16. SGPA & CGPA Calculation:
- SGPA = (Sum of Credits * Grade Points) / (Total Semester Credits)
- CGPA = (Sum of Credits * Grade Points for all courses) / (Total Accumulated Credits)
17. B.Tech Degree Eligibility Requirements:
- Earn minimum prescribed total credits (160 credits).
- Minimum CGPA of 5.0.
- No outstanding dues (Institute, Library, Hostels).
- No pending disciplinary actions.
18. B.Tech (Honors) Degree Eligibility Requirements:
- SGPA >= 8.0 in first four semesters.
- Completed 4 additional approved MOOC/NPTEL courses (3 credits each = 12 credits) starting from 5th semester.
- SGPA >= 8.5 from 5th to 8th semesters.
- Overall CGPA >= 8.5 across all semesters.
- No backlogs and no disciplinary actions.

title: Exam Conduct, Malpractices, Penalties, Appellate Committee & Scholarships
text:
20. Exam Conduct: Strict discipline. Disciplinary committee handles academic dishonesty.
21. Malpractice Rules & Punishments:
- Taking answer booklet outside: 'M' Grade in subject.
- Verbal communication after 1 warning: Answer script taken away, asked to leave hall.
- Possession of unauthorized material / mobile phones / programmable calculators / copying: Zero marks in continuous eval; 'I' Grade in end-sem (eligible for makeup).
- Possession/exchange of another candidate's answer book: Zero marks & 'I' Grade in subject.
- Misbehavior, threatening invigilator, repeated offences: Cancellation of all theory exams in semester + debarred for 1 year (2 semesters).
- Impersonation: Handed over to police; cancellation of all exams + debarred for 2 years for both impersonator and candidate.
- Physical assault: RUSTICATION from Institute.
22. Certificate Retention Fee charged as per norms.
23. Academic Appellate Committee: Dean Academics (Convener), Dean Student Welfare, HoD.
24. Scholarships: Institute does not offer direct institute scholarship; students can avail Central/State Govt scholarships.

title: Hostel Management, Accommodation, Allotment & Exemption
text:
1. Hostel Management: Managed by Hostel Administration Committee (HAC) including Chief Warden, Warden, Assistant Warden, Caretaker, and Student Secretaries (Hostel, Cultural, Sports, Mess).
2. Accommodation: Available to B.Tech students during working academic year only. Must vacate rooms before vacations (unless permission granted for project/institute work). PhD scholars get hostel up to max 5 years.
3. Conditions of Allotment: Personal Data Form with parent contact required. Standard room inventory: cot, table, chair, ceiling fan, tube light. Room changes not permitted normally. Room vacating slip in triplicate.
4. Exemption from Residence: Married/Research/QIP scholars provided campus quarters are exempted. Day scholars/exemption granted by Chief Warden if shortage of rooms.

title: Hostel Code of Conduct, Girls In-Timing (10:00 PM), Room Upkeep & Property Damage
text:
5.1 Maintain courteous behavior inside and outside campus.
5.2 Must carry valid Institute ID card at all times.
5.3 Keep rooms and common areas clean. No pasting/scribbling on walls.
5.4 Girls In-Timing: All girl students must be inside the hostel before 10:00 PM. Prior permission from Warden required to stay away during weekends/holidays.
5.5 - 5.11 Room upkeep is personal responsibility. No screening pirated/unlicensed movies. Damage to room/furniture recovered from occupants or collective fine on hostel. No moving furniture or tampering with electrical fittings.
5.12 Must sign Hostel Upkeep Undertaking form.

title: Anti-Ragging Regulations, UGC Guidelines & Severe Punishments
text:
5.13 Ragging is totally banned and a criminal offence under IPC & UGC Regulations 2009.
5.14 Definition of Ragging: Any conduct teasing, handling with rudeness, rowdism, causing psychological harm, physical abuse, extortion, forced acts, or disrupting academic activity of freshers.
- Protection for Informants: Students reporting ragging are protected.
- 1st Year Protection: First year UG students are lodged in separate fenced hostels; seniors are strictly denied entry.
- Punishments for Ragging:
  i) Suspension from classes and academic privileges.
  ii) Withholding scholarships/fellowships.
  iii) Debarring from tests/exams.
  iv) Withholding results.
  v) Debarring from representing institute in sports/meets.
  vi) Suspension/expulsion from hostel.
  vii) Cancellation of admission.
  viii) Rustication for 1 to 4 semesters.
  ix) Expulsion from institute & debarring from admission to other institutions, plus collective punishment if culprits not identified.

title: Smoking/Alcohol Ban, Electrical Appliances Ban, Vehicle Ban, Guests & Responsibilities
text:
5.15 Smoking, Alcohol & Narcotics: STRICTLY PROHIBITED in campus and hostels. Possession or consumption leads to IMMEDIATE EXPULSION from hostel and RUSTICATION from Institute. Entire campus is a smoke-free zone.
6. Guests & Visitors: Guest stay max 1 week with prior Warden approval on payment. No overnight guests in student rooms. Men visiting women's hostel and vice-versa is strictly restricted.
8. Appliances & Cooking: Electric heaters, immersion rods, electric stoves, and electric irons are FORBIDDEN in rooms. Private cooking in rooms is strictly forbidden (appliances confiscated + fine).
9. Collective Responsibilities:
- Powered vehicles (bikes/cars) for students are COMPLETELY BANNED on campus. Violating vehicles will be confiscated until course completion with heavy penal charges.
- Cycles must be parked in designated parking only.
- Students going outside should return to campus before 10:00 PM.
- No picnics without Dean Student Welfare permission. No organizing unauthorized meetings/functions.

title: Mess Rules, Compulsory Dining, Rebate / Reduction Policy (N-2 Days)
text:
11. Mess Rules:
11.1 All hostel residents must be members of a hostel mess. Must carry ID card & mess card.
11.2 Permanent membership for semester. Mess change only for 2nd year UG onwards senior boys.
11.9 - 11.10 Self-service system; unlimited food except special items. No wasting food.
11.21 No food or utensils (plates, spoons, tumblers) allowed outside mess/in rooms (unless sick with Medical Officer certificate).
11.11 - 11.17 Mess Reduction (Rebate) Policy:
- Admissible Grounds: Approved study holidays/semester vacations, HoD-recommended sports/competitions/educational tours, placement interviews/internships, hospitalization due to serious illness.
- Application Deadline: Apply in prescribed form 3 DAYS IN ADVANCE forwarded by Warden, and sign the Mess Leaving Register.
- Calculation Formula: Entitled to reduction ONLY for (N - 2) days, where N is the total number of days absent from the mess.
- Medical Leave from native place: Must intimate Mess Manager by post before holiday expiry with doctor's certificate (Civil Asst Surgeon or higher).
11.20 Cooking in rooms is strictly forbidden.

title: Roll Call Extension (till 11:00 PM) & First Year UG Hostel Special Rules
text:
13. Roll Call Extension Rules:
- Extension granted for club work and festival teams till 11:00 PM (conducted in Admin building).
- Apply to Warden before 4:00 PM on the day with staff advisor permission letter.
- Girls roll call extension after 10:00 PM uses biometric system and intimation to warden & parents. (Min 3 girls per club/team).
14. Special Rules for ALL First Year UG Hostels:
14.1 Must enter hostel before 9:30 PM. Latecomers banned from outings for 1 week (doubled on repetition).
14.2 Compulsory roll call by 10:00 PM.
14.3 Maintain silence after 10:00 PM.
14.4 Mandatory entry in IN/OUT register when leaving campus.
14.5 No tobacco/alcohol/drugs.
14.7 No corridor games except indoor board games (chess/carrom).
14.8 Birthday parties and celebrations inside hostel are NOT ALLOWED.
14.9 Hostel terrace is strictly out of bounds.
14.12 Dress Code: Sleeveless dress is NOT permitted in the mess.
14.13 Anti-Ragging Separation: First year students are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from visiting senior hostels. Violators face suspension from hostel.

title: Women's Cell (POSH), Grievance Cell, RTI, Reservation & Student Disciplinary Code
text:
15. Women's Cell: Constituted under Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, Redressal) Act 2013. Gender-neutral policy covering physical advances, sexual remarks, stalking, voyeurism, exhibitionism, offensive work environment. Criminal offences result in academic termination/suspension.
16. Grievance Cell: Redresses student grievances, suggestion boxes, email to officer in-charge.
17. RTI Cell: RTI Act 2005 compliance (www.iiitu.ac.in/rti.html).
18. Reservation Cell: UGC/AICTE norms.
STUDENT CONDUCT & DISCIPLINARY CODE (Sections 1-15):
- Applicable to all students across all campus activities.
- Prohibited: Groupism, mobile phones in classrooms/labs/exam halls, anti-institutional/political agitations, strikes, gherao, damaging property, weapons/explosives, rash driving, unauthorized outsiders.
- Sanctions:
  * Minor: Formal warning letter.
  * Major: Debarring from exams, Suspension (with loss of attendance for suspension period), Restitution (compensating property damage / physical injury), Forfeiture of caution deposit, Expulsion (permanent dismissal).
- Functionaries: HoDs/Wardens impose minor sanctions; Dean Student Welfare recommends major sanctions; Director is ultimate authority for major sanctions.
- Right to Appeal: Appeal against authority lies to Director; appeal against Director lies to Senate (Senate decision is final).
